title: Safety Culture and Human Factors in Foreign Object Management in Surgery
content: This paper examines the human and safety culture factors of the seemingly intractable problem of foreign object retention in surgery. It reports the findings of the FOR-RaM research project, which sought to discover challenges to Foreign Object Management across surgical and maternity settings in Irish hospitals and to recommend changes to address these challenges. This was a co-design partnership with a wide range of stakeholders in the study hospital; its mixed methods included Semi-structured interviews, Observations in surgical settings and Action Learning Sets. The results highlight a number of safety culture and human factors considerations which may facilitate or hinder Foreign Object Management, such as (individual and team) Goals, the Processes required for successful Foreign Object Management, Culture, Teamwork, Information Management and Training.
